domain_definition: A domain is a governed graph region with context objects, roles, templates, proof obligations, authority boundaries, receipt paths, settlement rules, and fission triggers.

domains.name: Continuity Substrate
domains.purpose: Govern import, classification, settlement, receipt issuance, and inheritance bundle generation.
proof_obligations: Every accepted object must cite a settlement receipt.
Every excluded object must carry a non-inheritable status and exclusion reason.
Every inheritance bundle must list included objects, excluded objects, and the receipts justifying inclusion.
Accepted state changes must be explicit, never inferred from fluent output.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can mark candidate, accepted, rejected, deferred, or needs_review within local continuity state; cannot certify external truth or legal compliance.
settlement_rules: Candidate imports are witness-only until settled.
Accepted objects may be inherited only through receipt citation.
Rejected objects remain available as witness but cannot be included in the next-session context bundle.
Deferred objects require a follow-up task or explicit human review before inheritance.
fission_triggers: Settlement rules diverge for operational tasks, demo claims, and external integrations.
Receipts become too broad to explain a single accepted-state change.
Trace output becomes noisy enough that reviewers cannot distinguish accepted state from witness material.

domains.name: Generative Governance
domains.purpose: Derive governed work structure from an objective before carriers act.
proof_obligations: Objective routes must state implicated domains and why each domain is needed.
Generated roles must have authority ceilings and proof requirements.
Work packets must include bounded context and expected return schema.
Fission recommendations must cite concrete overload signals.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can propose domains, roles, packets, and routes; cannot treat carrier output as accepted state.
settlement_rules: A generated work structure is candidate until reviewed or accepted by settlement.
Carrier branches return to settlement rather than mutating accepted context directly.
Fission proposals require receipt-backed evidence before changing the domain registry.
fission_triggers: Role derivation repeatedly creates unrelated role families inside one domain.
Proof obligations split into incompatible classes.
The same objective frequently routes across more neighboring domains than local templates.

domains.name: Capability Routing
domains.purpose: Match governed work packets to lawful execution surfaces such as Gemini, Codex CLI, local scripts, MongoDB MCP, Google Cloud, or human review.
proof_obligations: Route decisions must cite required capabilities and authority limits.
Side-effecting routes must state whether human approval is required.
External API routes must record which credentials or secrets were required without exposing secret values.
Carrier outputs must return to settlement before inheritance.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can select or recommend a carrier; cannot grant a carrier direct authority over accepted state beyond its work packet.
settlement_rules: Read-only routes may return evidence directly to settlement.
Write routes must include mutation target, rollback or cleanup path, and proof artifact.
Failed routes create diagnostic receipts rather than silent retries.
fission_triggers: Carrier-specific setup overwhelms route policy.
Google Cloud, MongoDB, and local CLI routes require distinct proof models.
Human review paths require workflow states not shared with automated carriers.

domains.name: MCP Visibility
domains.purpose: Prove governed retrieval: what was considered, returned, excluded, and cited for inheritance.
proof_obligations: Trace must list considered, returned, and excluded objects.
Every returned object must cite a receipt.
Trace must state accepted_state_changed.
Trace must state external_mutation_attempted.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can expose retrieval visibility; cannot promote retrieved objects to accepted state.
settlement_rules: Accepted objects are returned only when receipt-backed.
Excluded witness remains inspectable in trace metadata.
Trace generation must be read-only unless an explicit seed or migration task is active.
fission_triggers: Trace needs differ between local JSON, MongoDB Atlas, and external MCP server surfaces.
Retrieval policies become domain-specific.
Auditors require graph-level queries beyond visibility trace fields.

domains.name: Enterprise Trust
domains.purpose: Represent receipt-backed auditability, authority boundaries, graph traceability, and non-claims for enterprise AI work.
proof_obligations: Audit answers must trace inherited objects to settlement decisions.
Claims must be marked as proven, roadmap, local-only, external-only, or unsupported.
Compliance claims must remain non-claims unless reviewed by qualified external authority.
Authority boundaries must be stated for agents, humans, scripts, and external systems.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can provide technical audit substrate and claim status; cannot certify regulatory compliance.
settlement_rules: Enterprise-facing claims require proof references and non-claim boundaries.
Receipt chains must preserve rejected and deferred witness as non-inheritable context.
Audit exports are read-only unless a separate release receipt accepts them.
fission_triggers: Customer-specific policy models are needed.
Audit query volume requires a dedicated graph index or materialized view.
Compliance review workflows require external reviewer roles.

domains.name: Google Cloud Runtime
domains.purpose: Package and deploy the dAimon vertical slice to Google infrastructure while preserving receipt boundaries.
proof_obligations: Deployment must cite source commit, image digest or build id, environment variables used by name, and health check result.
Secrets must be referenced by secret name or environment key, not exposed in committed files.
Runtime endpoints must expose accepted-only inheritance behavior or a documented local equivalent.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can deploy contest runtime when credentials are available; cannot claim production hardening without hardening tests.
settlement_rules: A deployment is accepted only after health check and receipt generation.
Failed deployments produce diagnostic receipts and do not advance demo proof.
Runtime config changes require explicit release packaging.
fission_triggers: Cloud Run runtime and Agent Builder integration need separate lifecycle controls.
Deployment credentials differ from runtime application credentials.
Monitoring and audit export become large enough for independent ownership.

domains.name: Self-Demonstrating Video Agent
domains.purpose: Govern the creation of the contest demo video as receipt-bearing AI work.
proof_obligations: Every spoken product claim must be marked as proven, local proof, live proof, roadmap, or non-claim.
Every demo scene must cite the artifact it shows or state that it is conceptual.
The final video package must include a claim audit receipt.
Non-claims must be explicit for production readiness, legal compliance, and full Google/MongoDB integration.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can produce demo assets and claim audit receipts; cannot convert roadmap statements into proven claims.
settlement_rules: Unsupported claims are removed or marked roadmap before release.
A shot is accepted only when it maps to an artifact, a live screen, or an explicit conceptual label.
The submission bundle is accepted only after claim audit passes.
fission_triggers: Video production assets become large enough to require media pipeline ownership.
Claim auditing and creative direction require separate review cycles.
Submission packaging diverges from ongoing product documentation.

domains.name: ION Product Boundary
domains.purpose: Keep dAimon legible as the product surface while preserving ION as the deeper law, engine, and continuity organism.
proof_obligations: Every public claim must distinguish dAimon product behavior from deeper ION research substrate.
Imported ION modules must state what product capability they expose.
The contest slice must not imply that the full ION organism has been shipped.
Product docs must preserve the line that dAimon is ION made legible, usable, and shippable.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can define product boundary and module import posture; cannot claim all ION capabilities are implemented in dAimon.
settlement_rules: ION-derived capabilities are product claims only after dAimon proof artifacts exist.
Unimplemented ION depth remains roadmap or architecture.
Contest-facing language must be settled against current evidence before release.
fission_triggers: Public product messaging and internal ION engineering require separate ownership.
Module import planning becomes detailed enough to need independent migration receipts.
Customer-facing product boundary diverges from research architecture.

domains.name: Dynamic Technology Fabric
domains.purpose: Govern external technologies through adapter manifests, normalized objects, authority classification, proof requirements, and receipt-backed inheritance.
proof_obligations: Every adapter must state readable objects, writable objects, required authority, proof returned, and stale or secret-bearing risk.
Every cross-surface copy, index, embedding, summary, or graph link must preserve source lineage.
Overlapping surfaces must use explicit edges such as same_as, copied_from, indexed_from, embedded_from, summarized_from, supersedes, conflicts_with, or source_of_truth.
Adapter output remains candidate until settled.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can register and normalize adapters; cannot treat a connected system as equally authoritative without settlement.
settlement_rules: Adapter manifests are accepted only after structural validation.
Normalized objects inherit no more authority than their source path and proof allow.
Conflicting surfaces route to settlement rather than automatic merge.
fission_triggers: Adapter classes need provider-specific credentials, tests, and proof models.
Vector, graph, relational, and SaaS connectors require different normalization rules.
Overlap settlement becomes complex enough to require a dedicated lineage domain.

domains.name: Portable Continuation
domains.purpose: Let work move across conversations, devices, models, and local machines without losing receipt-backed context or proof boundaries.
proof_obligations: Every portable package must include accepted context, excluded witness, receipt citations, and authority scope.
Every replay must record carrier, project lane, packet nonce, and accepted-state boundary.
A new carrier session may inherit only what the package permits.
Continuation failures must produce diagnostic receipts rather than silent context reconstruction.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can package and replay governed context; cannot make a new carrier trust unsafely inherited chat history.
settlement_rules: Portable context packages are read-only exports unless a return packet is settled.
Carrier returns are candidate transitions until settlement.
Stale continuation packages require refresh or caveat preservation.
fission_triggers: Mobile, browser, local CLI, and cloud carriers require distinct package formats.
Replay receipts become large enough for independent audit tooling.
Project identity and continuation packaging need separate authority policies.

domains.name: Voice To Local Work
domains.purpose: Convert voice-derived intent into bounded packets for local PC and Codex/ION execution while preserving confirmation gates for high-risk phrases.
proof_obligations: Voice-derived instructions must record transcript source, confidence if available, risk phrase matches, and confirmation status.
High-risk phrases such as attack, exploit, bypass, delete, exfiltrate, credentials, secrets, wipe, push, deploy, production, red team, or break into require confirmation before execution.
Local execution packets must state project lane, allowed path, authority ceiling, and proof return schema.
No high-risk action may run from unconfirmed voice intent.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can transform voice into candidate packets; cannot execute high-risk local or cloud actions without confirmation and settlement.
settlement_rules: Ambiguous voice intent creates a clarification receipt.
Confirmed low-risk voice packets may route to local work under normal packet rules.
High-risk packets remain blocked until explicit confirmation is receipted.
fission_triggers: Speech recognition confidence and intent parsing need separate model evaluation.
Mobile UX requires independent product ownership.
Local connector execution policy becomes complex enough for a dedicated local-control domain.

domains.name: Security And Red-Team Containment
domains.purpose: Test trust-breaking scenarios in containment lanes using synthetic secrets, synthetic repos/databases, bounded scenarios, incident receipts, patches, and re-tests.
proof_obligations: High-risk tests must run only against explicit lab targets with synthetic secrets or sandbox resources.

Prompt injection, malicious tool output, stale inheritance, secret leakage, unsafe file access, confused authority, false receipts, impersonation, unbounded execution, permission drift, database mutation accidents, and cross-agent poisoning must be tracked as threat classes.
Every incident report must state blast radius, detector result, containment action, patch plan, and re-test requirement.
Security tests must not be confused with authorization to attack real systems.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can design and run bounded lab scenarios; cannot run high-risk tests against real user, cloud, database, or public systems without explicit containment approval.
settlement_rules: Lab scenarios are accepted only when target, synthetic data, and containment boundary are documented.
Findings become candidate patches until implemented and re-tested.
Containment receipts must preserve what was attempted and what was blocked.
fission_triggers: Threat model registry becomes larger than the product ops domain can own.
Sandbox cloud/database probes require separate infrastructure.
Incident response and detector engineering diverge.

domains.name: Project Identity And Collaboration
domains.purpose: Create project-bound first contact packages, pairing proofs, invite capabilities, and collaborator roles so the project lane remains the shared object rather than a chat transcript.
proof_obligations: A project ID is a routing identifier, not full authority.
Pairing secrets or local hub proof are required before queueing bounded packets or touching local project files.
Invite tokens must carry scope such as viewer, contributor, builder, reviewer, authorizer, or owner.
Every collaborator action must be receipted and settled before accepted state changes.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can create project lanes, pairing packages, and scoped invites; cannot grant high-risk mutation authority without local proof or human approval.
settlement_rules: First contact packages create project identity and initial receipt only.
Project ID alone may expose only public/basic metadata.
Capability tokens scope actions, and settlement decides what becomes shared accepted state.
fission_triggers: Enterprise teams require user identity, billing, or admin policy.
Local hub proof and cloud hub proof need different trust models.
Collaboration roles expand into full access-control management.

domains.name: Product Operations
domains.purpose: Manage repo work, issue flow, release gates, validation cadence, and public proof packaging.
proof_obligations: Each roadmap phase must have dependencies, evidence, tests, and exit criteria.
Release candidates must record validation commands and results.
Public artifacts must separate proven behavior from product vision.
Credentials and secrets must stay out of committed files.
domains.authority_ceiling: Can coordinate build and release process; cannot bypass settlement requirements for demo claims.
settlement_rules: A task closes only when evidence and validation are attached.
A release advances only when required validation gates pass or exceptions are documented.
Roadmap changes are accepted through explicit plan receipts or commits.
fission_triggers: Operational backlog splits into engineering, cloud, demo, and submission lanes.
Validation gates require separate automation ownership.
Public release materials require a dedicated communications domain.
